findings.title: Authorization check is wrong: attendees and non-owner admins can modify bookings
Wrong credentials and user used for the calendar update
Guest dedup and blacklist checks are case-sensitive, and duplicates within the input are not removed
Email logic sends the wrong template to guests and compares emails case-sensitively; the full guest list is passed instead of the filtered one
Client-side validation rejects valid input and the error handler can show a wrong message
MultiEmail imports from the "@calcom/ui" barrel inside the ui package, and the "Remove email" tooltip is not localized

response:
## 1) Severity: CRITICAL | Type: Security
Title: Authorization check is wrong: attendees and non-owner admins can modify bookings

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-56

Explanation:
`isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&`, so a user must be both admin and owner. That wrongly denies plain admins and is inconsistent with the name. The `isAttendee` check lets any attendee add arbitrary guests to the organizer's booking. The attendee match is by email, and `user.email` may be unverified or secondary. The booking is then updated with the organizer's calendar credentials, and emails are sent to arbitrary addresses, so this can be used for spam. Also, when `teamId` is missing the code calls `isTeamAdmin(user.id, 0)`, which is a pointless query. Use `||`, skip the team check when there is no team, and decide deliberately whether attendees should be allowed.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const teamId = booking.eventType?.teamId;
const isTeamAdminOrOwner = teamId
  ? (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) || (await isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId))
  : false;
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Wrong credentials and user used for the calendar update

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158-165

Explanation:
`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({...user})` use the acting user's credentials, not the booking organizer's. When an admin or attendee adds guests, the calendar event is updated with the wrong credentials, or not at all. The booking already includes `booking.user.credentials`, so use the organizer's. Also, `updateCalendarAttendees` is not wrapped in try/catch, so a calendar failure after the DB write returns an error even though the guests were already saved.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...booking.user!, credentials: booking.user!.credentials });
try { await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking); } catch (e) { /* log */ }
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Guest dedup and blacklist checks are case-sensitive, and duplicates within the input are not removed

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70-78

Explanation:
The blacklist is lowercased, but the guest is compared as-is, so `Foo@X.com` bypasses it. Comparison against existing attendees is also case-sensitive. Duplicates within the input are only checked on the client, so the server can insert duplicate attendees. Normalize guests to lowercase and dedupe them on the server.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const normalized = [...new Set(guests.map((g) => g.toLowerCase()))];
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Email logic sends the wrong template to guests and compares emails case-sensitively; the full guest list is passed instead of the filtered one

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168
- packages/emails/email-manager.ts:539-547

Explanation:
`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the raw input, including guests that were filtered out as blacklisted or already present. Existing attendees whose emails are in that list receive the "scheduled" email again, and blacklisted guests are not in `attendees`. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead. Also, errors are swallowed with a `console.log` that drops the error object.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, uniqueGuests);
~~~

## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Client-side validation rejects valid input and the error handler can show a wrong message

Affected:
- apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-58
- apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42-45

Explanation:
The initial state is `[""]`. If the user leaves an empty field, validation fails, and the error never clears after the input is corrected or the dialog is cancelled and reopened. The `isInvalidEmail` flag is not reset on success. `onError` builds the message as `${code}: ${t(message)}`, which is always truthy, so the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is dead code. The schema is also recreated on every render.

Proposed fix:
Move the schema to module scope, filter out empty strings before validating, reset `isInvalidEmail` on success, and use `err.message ? t(err.message) : t("unable_to_add_guests")`.

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: MultiEmail imports from the "@calcom/ui" barrel inside the ui package, and the "Remove email" tooltip is not localized

Affected:
- packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:1-2
- packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:46

Explanation:
Importing from the package's own index risks circular imports. The `Tooltip` content is a hardcoded English string. The list uses `key={index}`, which causes wrong input state when items are removed.

Proposed fix:
Use relative imports and `t("remove_email")`.

The golden comment specifically explains that the blacklist is lowercased but input emails are not, and the candidate correctly identifies this as a case-sensitivity issue that allows bypasses like 'Foo@X.com'. true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

Both comments point to the same logical operator bug that would wrongly deny access to plain admins.
